newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak stats bureau sees 5.7-6.3 pct H1 GDP growth. [CORRECTED 13:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Slovak stats bureau sees 5.7-6.3 pct H1 GDP growth. [CORRECTED 13:15 GMT]

text.p: The Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) said on Wednesday real GDP growth in the first half of 1997 should range between 5.7 and 6.3 percent, after real growth of 7.1 percent in the same period of 1996.
It added that average inflation for the first half should be 6.0-6.4 percent year-on-year, compared to average first half inflation of 6.2 percent last year.
Real GDP growth for 1996 was 6.8 percent, compared with 7.4 percent in 1995. (Corrects real GDP growth for 1996 from 6.9 percent to 6.8 percent.)

SUSR Deputy Chairman Milutin Kristofic said the bureau expected real industrial output to grow between 4.0 and 4.4 percent, year-on-year, in the first half, while the unemployment rate by the end of June should be 12.8 percent, up slightly from 12.4 percent at the end of June 1996.

"The range in our forecasts represents a difference between two methods of calculations; SUSR's own statistical forecasts and a model-based prognosis from our economic analysis unit, Infostat," Kristofic said, without elaborating further.
